text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose slightly today, gaining about 0.66%, as crude oil prices stabilized following a week of volatility tied to U.S.-Iran tensions. The stock had fallen sharply earlier in the week—from $424.89 on September 18th to $389.68 by September 22nd—but has recovered modestly over the past two trading days as geopolitical risk receded. U.S. crude sits at $96.41 per barrel, and refineries are running at 94% capacity, which supports refining margins.

The broader context here is that oil prices swung significantly based on ceasefire negotiations between the U.S. and Iran last week; crude fell nearly 8% for the week as talks progressed, then began recovering when the Trump administration rejected Iran's conditional ceasefire proposal. Refiner stocks like Marathon tend to benefit when crude prices fall (because their input costs drop faster than product prices fall) and stabilize when geopolitical risk becomes clearer—even if that clarity points to renewed tension. The stock's modest bounce today reflects a market settling into the reality of renewed U.S.-Iran friction, rather than a collapse into unknown risk.
